title: Efficient End-to-end Language Model Fine-tuning on Graphs

problem.claim: Language-model approaches for exploiting text information in text-attributed graphs have computation- and data-efficiency challenges.

gap.claim: Existing approaches suffer from inferior computation and data efficiency.

contributions.claim: LEADING is an end-to-end language-model fine-tuning approach for text-attributed graphs.
LEADING uses semi-supervised end-to-end training of language models and graph neural networks to transfer language-model knowledge with limited labeled data.
LEADING introduces neighbor decoupling for language models and implicit graph modeling for graph neural networks to address computation efficiency.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe LEADING as a novel approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art results on the ogbn-arxiv leaderboard.
The authors report computation cost and memory overhead comparable to graph-less language-model fine-tuning.
The authors report superior computation and data efficiency through comprehensive experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-attributed graphs have broad real-world applications, and language models may replace shallow text embeddings in graph neural networks.
Existing language-model approaches for graphs are described as inefficient in computation and data usage.
The study introduces LEADING for efficient end-to-end language-model fine-tuning on text-attributed graphs.
The authors report strong leaderboard performance, comparable computational and memory overhead, and improved efficiency across experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the full set of datasets, language models, graph tasks, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details or experimental protocol.
